raw_response:
I will keep my full 4.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because my land is small, I already know this system well, and I have a well for irrigation, so this is the safest way for me to keep grain output stable. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because on a small farm I need steady yield more than anything else. For wheat, I will put moderate fertilizer and irrigate a few times, mainly at the key stages, because wheat in my area responds well to water and nitrogen but too much input wastes money. For maize, I will also use moderate fertilizer, with nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, because maize needs strong growth after wheat harvest and hybrid seed can make better use of fertilizer. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and common for my scale, and it saves labor compared with deeper tillage. I will spray pesticides only when needed but I still plan for a few applications, because I do not want weeds, insects, or disease to reduce yield on such limited land. My aim this year is stable production, manageable labor, and controlled cost.
